This term leverages the correlation between shading and surface normals to enforce local smoothness, weighted by geometric proximity and orientation [S1].

The claim states that the term leverages the correlation between shading and surface normals to enforce local smoothness, weighted by geometric proximity and orientation. The evidence in Source [S1] explicitly defines a 'Shading-Normal consistency loss' ($L_{sn}$). The formula for $L_{sn}$ includes: 1) $|S(r) - S(r')|$ representing the difference in shading (smoothness/consistency), 2) $omega_n(r, r')$ which measures the cosine similarity of normals (orientation), and 3) $(1 - tanh(Dis(r, r')))$ which acts as a weight based on the distance between 3D points (geometric proximity). The text also states 'Since shading and surface normal are correlated...'. Thus, every fact in the claim is present in the evidence.
